records.name: Typed relational bridge composition
records.statement: If B1 and B2 have matching intermediate type and version, nonempty scope intersection, and every intermediate output of B1 lies in the domain of B2, then their ordinary relational composite is a well-defined bridge from the source of B1 to the target of B2.
nonclaims: Type-correct composition does not imply semantic equivalence, truth preservation, or physical validity.

records.name: Composite preservation is intersection-bounded
records.statement: Under the BridgeCore conservative composition contract, the structure automatically preserved by B2 o B1 is exactly P1 intersect P2.
hypotheses: B1 and B2 are composable BridgeCore bridges
preserved structure uses a shared declared label vocabulary
nonclaims: This does not forbid a separately proved reconstruction theorem; it forbids silently assuming one.

records.name: Loss is monotone under ordinary composition
records.statement: For the conservative composite L21 = L1 union (P1 minus P2), every structure already lost by B1 remains lost in B2 o B1, and every structure preserved by B1 but not B2 becomes lost in the composite.
hypotheses: B1 and B2 are composable BridgeCore bridges
nonclaims: Deterministic post-processing is not automatically exact reconstruction of discarded structure.

records.name: Identity bridge is neutral under complete structure tracking
records.statement: For a compatible bridge B, an identity bridge whose tracked structure vocabulary is exactly P_B union L_B composes neutrally with B at the relation and preservation/loss metadata levels.
hypotheses: identity bridge and B satisfy ordinary composition compatibility
the identity bridge tracked structure set equals P_B union L_B
nonclaims: A bridge is not an identity merely because source and target type names happen to match; partial structure metadata does not imply two-sided metadata neutrality.

records.name: Compatible BridgeCore composition is associative
records.statement: For three mutually compatible bridges, ordinary relational composition, scope intersection, preservation intersection, and conservative loss propagation are associative.
hypotheses: all intermediate type/version/domain conditions required by both parenthesizations hold
all required scope intersections are nonempty
nonclaims: Associativity of the structural bridge calculus does not imply that an application-specific interpretation is associative or lossless.

records.name: Same endpoint types do not determine one bridge
records.statement: Two bridges with the same source and target type/version can differ in relation, injectivity, and preserved/lost structure.
records.fixture: two-state identity transport versus two-state collapse transport
nonclaims: The fixture is synthetic and does not model a particular physical channel.

records.name: Version mismatch blocks composition
records.statement: Two individually valid bridges fail the BridgeCore composition predicate when the first target version differs from the second source version.
records.fixture: A@1 -> B@1 followed by B@2 -> C@1
nonclaims: A separately supplied migration bridge may make two versions compatible.

records.name: Disjoint scope blocks composition
records.statement: Two otherwise type/version/domain-compatible bridges are not composable when their declared scopes have empty intersection.
records.fixture: calibration-A-only bridge followed by calibration-B-only bridge
nonclaims: Scope overlap is a licensing condition, not evidence that the bridge is physically correct.

records.name: Lossy transport plus deterministic decoder is not exact reconstruction
records.statement: A noninjective bridge followed by a deterministic canonical decoder can produce a total composite while failing to reconstruct distinct source states.
records.fixture: two-bit source -> first-bit projection -> canonical two-bit representative
nonclaims: This is a finite structural reconstruction counterexample, not an information-destruction claim about physics.
